findings.summary: No lower bound on `issuedAt`: an epoch-zero / far-past timestamp silently drops the edit
findings.evidence: `const at = new Date(Number.isNaN(issuedMs) ? now : Math.min(issuedMs, now));` clamps only the upper side. A Go zero time (`0001-01-01T00:00:00Z`, which `Date.parse` parses to a large negative ms) or any bogus-but-parseable past value yields `at` far in the past; `touchUpdatedAt` then matches nothing (`where updatedAt < at`) and the real edit never advances `updatedAt` — silently, since the return count is ignored. The sibling code path in `yorkie-admin.service.ts:274` (`parseTimestamp`) explicitly rejects `ms <= 0` for exactly this reason, so the webhook path is inconsistent with the established handling of Yorkie's "unset" timestamp. A `ms <= 0 → now` fallback would close it.

findings.summary: rawBody capture keyed on an exact path string; any URL variant (trailing slash, global prefix, proxy rewrite) makes every webhook 401 forever
findings.evidence: `if (req.url?.split('?', 1)[0] === YORKIE_WEBHOOK_PATH) req.rawBody = buf;` requires byte-exact `/internal/yorkie/events`. Express route matching is non-strict, so `POST /internal/yorkie/events/` (or a differently-cased/proxy-rewritten path) still reaches `YorkieEventController.handleEvent`, but `req.rawBody` is undefined and `YorkieSignatureGuard` (yorkie-signature.guard.ts:49) throws `UnauthorizedException('Missing webhook signature')`. The failure mode is total and silent: every event is rejected, `Document.updatedAt` never advances, list ordering degrades to creation order, and Yorkie retries with backoff — while the log message points at a signature problem rather than the missing raw body. The guard also cannot distinguish "raw body not captured" from "no signature sent", so the misconfiguration is undiagnosable from logs.

findings.summary: `touchUpdatedAt` rejection escapes the handler, contradicting the documented/asserted "always 200" contract
findings.evidence: `await this.documentService.touchUpdatedAt(parsed.id, at);` is not wrapped; a Prisma/DB error (connection loss, deadlock) propagates and Nest returns 500. The class doc comment and yorkie-event.controller.spec.ts:66 ("always answers ok so Yorkie does not retry") state the endpoint always answers ok — the test only covers the early-return branch, so the contract is unenforced on the one path that can actually throw. Whether retrying on a DB error is desirable or not, the code and its stated contract disagree, and the failure is also unlogged here.

findings.summary: Parsed key `type` is discarded, so a mismatched-type key touches the wrong document row
findings.evidence: `parseYorkieDocKey` returns `{ type, id }` but only `parsed.id` is used; `touchUpdatedAt(id, at)` filters on `id` alone. A key like `pdf-<sheetId>` (or any key whose prefix disagrees with the row's `type` column) will bump an unrelated document's `updatedAt`. Cheap fix: include `type: parsed.type` in the `updateMany` where-clause, making the operation self-validating rather than trusting the key's prefix.

findings.summary: Empty-data guard is key-count based, so a data object whose only keys are undefined still bumps `updatedAt`
findings.evidence: `Object.keys(data).length > 0 ? { ...data, updatedAt: new Date() } : data` counts keys, not defined values. `ApiV1DocumentsController.update` (api/v1/documents.controller.ts:79) passes the request body straight through as `data`, so a body such as `{"title":null}` or any unrecognized key yields length>0 and re-sorts the document to the top of the list (and, for an unknown key, Prisma throws afterwards). The new spec only covers `{}` and `{title:'New'}`, so this branch is untested.

findings.evidence: document.controller.ts:52-70 rewrote `attachMeta` (uses `d.updatedAt.toISOString()` and `yorkieAdminService.getEditors`) and lines 116/148 changed `orderBy` to `[{updatedAt:'desc'},{createdAt:'desc'}]`. The only spec for this controller, document.controller.spec.ts, covers just `createDocument` fileId gating; its mock even still stubs the now-unused `getSummaries` (line 13) rather than `getEditors`, so nothing would fail if `attachMeta` regressed (e.g. reverted to Yorkie's updatedAt, dropped editors, or lost the orderBy). Searched packages/backend/src/**/*.spec.ts and packages/backend/test/*.e2e-spec.ts for `updatedAt`/`getEditors` assertions — the e2e files only stub the service, they assert nothing about ordering.

The controller spec mocks `touchUpdatedAt` away entirely (yorkie-event.controller.spec.ts:9-12), so no test would catch dropping the `lt` filter and letting an out-of-order/duplicate webhook move `updatedAt` backwards.

findings.evidence: yorkie-event.controller.ts:19 says it is the only event type, while yorkie-event.controller.spec.ts:26-32 feeds a `DocumentWatched` event to assert it is ignored. findings.summary: Unauthenticated, throttle-exempt webhook endpoint accepts up to 25MB bodies — unbounded pre-auth resource consumption
findings.evidence: `@SkipThrottle()` (yorkie-event.controller.ts:32) removes the only global rate limit (ThrottlerGuard registered as APP_GUARD in app.module.ts:113, 120 req/60s). The route needs no JWT/API key, so any client that can reach the backend port hits it. Express body-parser runs *before* guards, and main.ts:47-56 applies `limit: JSON_BODY_LIMIT` (25MB default) to all JSON routes including this one, and additionally *retains* the raw buffer (`req.rawBody = buf`) only for this path — so each request pins the full 25MB buffer plus the parsed object until the guard rejects it, and the guard then computes an HMAC over those 25MB before rejecting. Attack: send many concurrent `POST /internal/yorkie/events` requests with 25MB JSON bodies and a garbage `X-Signature-256`; every request is fully buffered, doubled in memory, and HMAC'd with no rate limit → memory/CPU exhaustion of the backend. Nothing in the repo restricts the path at an ingress (no manifests present; the same process serves the public API on the same port). Mitigation would be a small per-route body limit (webhook payloads are a few hundred bytes) and/or a generous-but-finite throttle instead of a blanket skip.

findings.summary: Mass assignment into Prisma `updateDocument` on the v1 PATCH route (pre-existing, but it is the other call site of the method this diff changed)
findings.evidence: `update()` passes the raw request body straight through: `data: body` (api/v1/documents.controller.ts:77-80). The parameter is annotated with an inline TS type (`@Body() body: { title?: string }`), so the emitted `design:paramtypes` metadata is `Object` and the global ValidationPipe (main.ts:59-66, `whitelist`/`forbidNonWhitelisted`) skips validation entirely — those options only strip properties when the metatype is a decorated DTO class. Prisma accepts any valid `DocumentUpdateInput` at runtime, so an authenticated caller scoped to workspace A can PATCH one of its own documents with e.g. `{"workspace":{"connect":{"id":"<victim-workspace-id>"}}}` (moving attacker-controlled content into a workspace they are not a member of — WorkspaceScopeGuard only checks the route param, not the body), or `{"author":{"connect":{"id":1}}}` to forge authorship, or overwrite `id`/`fileId`. The sibling legacy route (document/document.controller.ts:183-196) does the safe thing and copies allowlisted fields; this one does not. The diff modifies `DocumentService.updateDocument` (document.service.ts:99-101) without narrowing this sink.

findings.summary: Webhook signature covers only the body — no timestamp/nonce, so a captured signed request can be replayed indefinitely
findings.evidence: `expected = sha256=HMAC(rawBody)` (yorkie-signature.guard.ts:53-55) binds nothing but the payload bytes: no `issuedAt` freshness window, no nonce cache, no binding to method/path. Anyone who observes one delivery (e.g. on the plaintext in-cluster hop documented in docs/design/documents-last-modified.md:69) can replay it forever. Impact is bounded because the only side effect is `touchUpdatedAt`, which is monotonic (document.service.ts:119-125) — a replay of an old event is a no-op and a replay of a recent one only re-sets the same value — so this is hardening, not an exploit. A freshness check on `body.attributes.issuedAt` (reject > N minutes old) would close it.

It is still fragile: adding `setGlobalPrefix`, an ingress path rewrite, or renaming the controller path silently turns every legitimate webhook into a 401 (Yorkie retry storm), and the pressure to 'fix' that is pressure to weaken the guard. Deriving the constant from the controller path, or matching case-insensitively with the trailing slash normalized, removes the coupling.

+# Lessons — Documents list `updatedAt` via Yorkie event webhook
+
+## Debug root cause with the live system, not just the code
+
+The two API samples the user pasted were byte-identical and stable — which
+looked like it *disproved* a per-request `updatedAt` flip. Reading the code
+alone couldn't resolve it. `kubectl logs` on the backend pod showed the
+`getSummaries` 800ms timeout firing ~every 5s poll, and a `port-forward` +
+timed `curl` proved the gateway RTT was ~25ms — so the slowness was the
+authenticated presence query straddling the 800ms cut, exactly the flip.
+The identical samples were just two "timeout → fallback" polls. **Measure the
+running system before committing to a mechanism.**
+
+## Don't propose a store you can't fill
+
+The first fix idea ("persist `updatedAt` in Postgres") was hollow until the
+user pushed: edits live only in Yorkie, so Postgres had no signal to write.
+The real design work was *how the value gets there* — the webhook — not the
+column. Verify the data flow feeding a field before proposing the field.
+
+## Verify the external contract from source, not memory
+
+Yorkie's event-webhook contract (event name `DocumentRootChanged`, payload
+shape, `X-Signature-256` = `sha256=hex(HMAC-SHA256(rawBody, project.SecretKey))`,
+at-least-once + throttled delivery) was read from the pinned `v0.7.12` tag via
+`gh api`, not guessed. The signing key being the *project secret key* is what
+let us reuse the existing `YORKIE_SECRET_KEY` with no new secret.
+
+## Implementation notes
+
+- HMAC must run over the **raw request bytes** — captured via
+  `bodyParser.json({ verify })`, not a re-serialized `@Body()` object.
+- Webhook receivers must be **idempotent + monotonic** (advance-only
+  `updateMany where updatedAt < at`) because delivery is at-least-once and
+  unordered; and **200-swallow** unrecognized input so the sender won't retry.
+- Prisma `@updatedAt` is the wrong tool when the app isn't on the write path —
+  use a plain `DateTime` column set explicitly.

+# Documents list `updatedAt` via Yorkie event webhook
+
+## Problem
+
+The documents list reorders every ~5s. Root cause (confirmed against the
+live cluster with `kubectl`): the list is sorted by `updatedAt`, which is
+layered on at request time from Yorkie's admin `GetDocuments`. That call
+times out at the backend's 800ms cut on essentially every poll (573
+timeouts / 68h; ~5.8s spacing = every refetch). The gateway RTT is ~25ms,
+so the slowness is the authenticated presence query against Yorkie's
+sharded MongoDB, and it straddles the 800ms cut — so `updatedAt` flips
+between the real Yorkie value and the `createdAt` fallback per poll, and
+the frontend re-sorts each time.
+
+Content edits are recorded **only in Yorkie** (the NestJS backend is not on
+the edit path), so Postgres has no last-modified signal today (`Document`
+has `createdAt` only).
+
+## Approach (Option A)
+
+Feed real edit times into Postgres via Yorkie's **event webhook**
+(`DocumentRootChanged`, fired on actual root-content operations). The list
+then reads/sorts a stable Postgres `updatedAt`; the flaky admin call is
+demoted to editor-avatars only and no longer affects ordering.
+
+Yorkie 0.7.12 contract (verified from source):
+- Event `DocumentRootChanged`; payload
+  `{ type, attributes: { key: "<type>-<id>", issuedAt } }`.
+- Header `X-Signature-256: sha256=<hex>`, `HMAC-SHA256(rawBody, project.SecretKey)`.
+  Signing key = project SecretKey = backend's existing `YORKIE_SECRET_KEY`.
+- At-least-once, throttled per document, retried w/ backoff → receiver must
+  be idempotent + monotonic.
+
+## Tasks
+
+- [x] Prisma: add `Document.updatedAt DateTime @default(now())` (manual, **not**
+      `@updatedAt`); migration backfills existing rows `= createdAt`.
+- [x] `yorkie-doc-key.ts`: add `parseYorkieDocKey(key) → { type, id } | null`.
+- [x] `DocumentService.touchUpdatedAt(id, at)` — monotonic advance-only
+      (`updateMany where updatedAt < at`), idempotent, no-op on missing doc.
+- [x] HMAC signature guard reading `req.rawBody` + `X-Signature-256`,
+      timing-safe compare against `YORKIE_SECRET_KEY`; reject if key unset.
+- [x] `main.ts`: capture raw body via `bodyParser.json({ verify })`.
+- [x] `POST /internal/yorkie/events` controller (no JWT, signature guard,
+      `@SkipThrottle`): handle `DocumentRootChanged`, parse key, touch;
+      200-swallow unknown keys/other events.
+- [x] `attachMeta`: source `updatedAt` from the DB column; keep `editors`
+      from the (best-effort) summary. Sort both list endpoints by
+      `[{ updatedAt: desc }, { createdAt: desc }]`.
+- [ ] **Ops (post-merge, needs cluster access)**: register webhook on the
+      Yorkie project (internal svc URL) — see design doc. Until this runs,
+      `updatedAt` stays at `createdAt` but the list is already stable.
+- [x] Tests: `parseYorkieDocKey` round-trip; guard valid/invalid/missing sig;
+      `touchUpdatedAt`/event handling (controller unit). *(DB-backed e2e for
+      the advance-only path deferred; covered by unit + monotonic SQL.)*
+
+## Review

+# Documents List — Last-Modified Ordering
+
+## Summary
+
+The documents list orders by "last modified". Content edits, however, flow
+**client → Yorkie only** — the NestJS backend is not on the edit path, so
+Postgres has no edit signal (`Document` historically had `createdAt` only).
+
+The list previously synthesized `updatedAt` per request from Yorkie's admin
+`GetDocuments` call. That call is slow and variable (authenticated presence
+query against a sharded MongoDB) and straddles the backend's 800 ms timeout,
+so `updatedAt` flipped between the real Yorkie value and a `createdAt`
+fallback on each 5 s poll — the list visibly reshuffled. (Confirmed on the
+live cluster: gateway RTT ~25 ms, but the admin query timed out ~every poll.)
+
+This design moves last-modified into a stable Postgres column fed by Yorkie's
+**event webhook**, and demotes the admin call to editor-avatars only.
+
+## Goals / Non-Goals
+
+**Goals**
+- Stable documents-list ordering that still reflects real edit recency.
+- No per-request dependency on the flaky Yorkie admin call for ordering.
+
+**Non-Goals**
+- Self-healing missed webhooks (backend down mid-edit) — accept small
+  staleness; a periodic Yorkie→PG sync can be layered later.
+- Fixing the underlying Yorkie admin-query latency (separate concern; the
+  "currently editing" avatars remain best-effort over it).
+
+## Proposal Details
+
+### Data model
+`Document.updatedAt DateTime @default(now())` — set **explicitly** (not
+Prisma `@updatedAt`). Migration backfills existing rows `= createdAt`. List
+endpoints order by `[{ updatedAt: desc }, { createdAt: desc }]`.
+
+### Ingestion — Yorkie event webhook (yorkie 0.7.12)
+- Event `DocumentRootChanged`, fired on real root-content operations (not
+  presence/attach/watch).
+- Body: `{ type, attributes: { key: "<type>-<id>", issuedAt } }`.
+- Auth: `X-Signature-256: sha256=<hex>`, `HMAC-SHA256(rawBody, project.SecretKey)`.
+  The signing key **is** the project secret key, already held by the backend
+  as `YORKIE_SECRET_KEY` — no new secret. Raw request bytes are captured via a
+  `bodyParser.json({ verify })` hook (HMAC must run over exact bytes).
+- Endpoint `POST /internal/yorkie/events` — no JWT, `YorkieSignatureGuard`,
+  `@SkipThrottle`. Parses the key (`parseYorkieDocKey`), then
+  `DocumentService.touchUpdatedAt(id, issuedAt)`.
+- Delivery is at-least-once, unordered, retried → `touchUpdatedAt` is
+  **monotonic** (`updateMany where updatedAt < at`) and idempotent; unknown
+  keys / other events / missing docs are 200-swallowed so Yorkie won't retry.
+
+### Read path
+`attachMeta` sources `updatedAt` from the DB column and uses
+`YorkieAdminService.getEditors` purely for the avatars. The frontend keeps its
+`updatedAt desc` default sort, which is now stable because the value is.
+
+### Ops
+Register the webhook on the Yorkie project (internal cluster URL, no public
+exposure):
+
+```
+yorkie project update <project> \
+  --event-webhook-url http://wafflebase.wafflebase.svc.cluster.local:3000/internal/yorkie/events \
+  --event-webhook-events DocumentRootChanged
+```
+
+### Non-content updates
+Rename / move never touch Yorkie, so no webhook fires. `DocumentService.updateDocument`
+therefore sets `updatedAt = now()` explicitly on every metadata update, so a
+rename still floats the document to the top like any edit.
+
+### Clock skew
+`issuedAt` is Yorkie's server clock. The webhook clamps it to `min(issuedAt, now())`
+before storing — a future-skewed event must not pin `updatedAt` ahead, which
+(with the monotonic guard) would reject every later real edit until wall-clock
+caught up.
+
+## Risks and Mitigation
+
+- **Duplicate / out-of-order events** → monotonic advance-only update absorbs.
+- **Forged requests** → HMAC signature verification is mandatory; the endpoint
+  refuses to run when `YORKIE_SECRET_KEY` is unset.
+- **`pdf` documents** have no CRDT edits → no webhook → stay at `createdAt`,
+  which is correct.
+- **Backfill of pre-deploy edit history** → the migration seeds existing rows to
+  `createdAt`, discarding any real Yorkie `updated_at`. Low impact in the current
+  deployment (the live admin read times out on ~every poll today, so the list
+  already effectively shows `createdAt` order), but not authoritative against a
+  healthy Yorkie. **Follow-up:** a one-time / periodic reconciliation job that
+  batch-reads Yorkie `updated_at` → `touchUpdatedAt` (Option C) both seeds
+  history and self-heals missed webhooks.
+- **Missed webhook** (backend down mid-edit, or Yorkie retries exhausted) →
+  `updatedAt` stays stale for that doc with no in-app recovery until its next
+  edit. Same reconciliation follow-up closes this.
+- **Deploy sequencing** → the list query reads/sorts the new column, so
+  `prisma migrate deploy` must run before the new image serves traffic, and the
+  Yorkie project webhook must be registered (see ops step) or `updatedAt` never
+  advances. Both are release-runbook items, not code paths.

+
+## Debug root cause with the live system, not just the code
+
+The two API samples the user pasted were byte-identical and stable — which
+looked like it *disproved* a per-request `updatedAt` flip. Reading the code
+alone couldn't resolve it. `kubectl logs` on the backend pod showed the
+`getSummaries` 800ms timeout firing ~every 5s poll, and a `port-forward` +
+timed `curl` proved the gateway RTT was ~25ms — so the slowness was the
+authenticated presence query straddling the 800ms cut, exactly the flip.
+The identical samples were just two "timeout → fallback" polls. **Measure the
+running system before committing to a mechanism.**
+
+## Don't propose a store you can't fill
+
+The first fix idea ("persist `updatedAt` in Postgres") was hollow until the
+user pushed: edits live only in Yorkie, so Postgres had no signal to write.
+The real design work was *how the value gets there* — the webhook — not the
+column. Verify the data flow feeding a field before proposing the field.
+
+## Verify the external contract from source, not memory
+
+Yorkie's event-webhook contract (event name `DocumentRootChanged`, payload
+shape, `X-Signature-256` = `sha256=hex(HMAC-SHA256(rawBody, project.SecretKey))`,
+at-least-once + throttled delivery) was read from the pinned `v0.7.12` tag via
+`gh api`, not guessed. The signing key being the *project secret key* is what
+let us reuse the existing `YORKIE_SECRET_KEY` with no new secret.
+
+## Implementation notes
+
+- HMAC must run over the **raw request bytes** — captured via
+  `bodyParser.json({ verify })`, not a re-serialized `@Body()` object.
+- Webhook receivers must be **idempotent + monotonic** (advance-only
+  `updateMany where updatedAt < at`) because delivery is at-least-once and
+  unordered; and **200-swallow** unrecognized input so the sender won't retry.
+- Prisma `@updatedAt` is the wrong tool when the app isn't on the write path —
+  use a plain `DateTime` column set explicitly.

+# Documents list `updatedAt` via Yorkie event webhook
+
+## Problem
+
+The documents list reorders every ~5s. Root cause (confirmed against the
+live cluster with `kubectl`): the list is sorted by `updatedAt`, which is
+layered on at request time from Yorkie's admin `GetDocuments`. That call
+times out at the backend's 800ms cut on essentially every poll (573
+timeouts / 68h; ~5.8s spacing = every refetch). The gateway RTT is ~25ms,
+so the slowness is the authenticated presence query against Yorkie's
+sharded MongoDB, and it straddles the 800ms cut — so `updatedAt` flips
+between the real Yorkie value and the `createdAt` fallback per poll, and
+the frontend re-sorts each time.
+
+Content edits are recorded **only in Yorkie** (the NestJS backend is not on
+the edit path), so Postgres has no last-modified signal today (`Document`
+has `createdAt` only).
+
+## Approach (Option A)
+
+Feed real edit times into Postgres via Yorkie's **event webhook**
+(`DocumentRootChanged`, fired on actual root-content operations). The list
+then reads/sorts a stable Postgres `updatedAt`; the flaky admin call is
+demoted to editor-avatars only and no longer affects ordering.
+
+Yorkie 0.7.12 contract (verified from source):
+- Event `DocumentRootChanged`; payload
+  `{ type, attributes: { key: "<type>-<id>", issuedAt } }`.
+- Header `X-Signature-256: sha256=<hex>`, `HMAC-SHA256(rawBody, project.SecretKey)`.
+  Signing key = project SecretKey = backend's existing `YORKIE_SECRET_KEY`.
+- At-least-once, throttled per document, retried w/ backoff → receiver must
+  be idempotent + monotonic.
+
+## Tasks
+
+- [x] Prisma: add `Document.updatedAt DateTime @default(now())` (manual, **not**
+      `@updatedAt`); migration backfills existing rows `= createdAt`.
+- [x] `yorkie-doc-key.ts`: add `parseYorkieDocKey(key) → { type, id } | null`.
+- [x] `DocumentService.touchUpdatedAt(id, at)` — monotonic advance-only
+      (`updateMany where updatedAt < at`), idempotent, no-op on missing doc.
+- [x] HMAC signature guard reading `req.rawBody` + `X-Signature-256`,
+      timing-safe compare against `YORKIE_SECRET_KEY`; reject if key unset.
+- [x] `main.ts`: capture raw body via `bodyParser.json({ verify })`.
+- [x] `POST /internal/yorkie/events` controller (no JWT, signature guard,
+      `@SkipThrottle`): handle `DocumentRootChanged`, parse key, touch;
+      200-swallow unknown keys/other events.
+- [x] `attachMeta`: source `updatedAt` from the DB column; keep `editors`
+      from the (best-effort) summary. Sort both list endpoints by
+      `[{ updatedAt: desc }, { createdAt: desc }]`.
+- [ ] **Ops (post-merge, needs cluster access)**: register webhook on the
+      Yorkie project (internal svc URL) — see design doc. Until this runs,
+      `updatedAt` stays at `createdAt` but the list is already stable.
+- [x] Tests: `parseYorkieDocKey` round-trip; guard valid/invalid/missing sig;
+      `touchUpdatedAt`/event handling (controller unit). *(DB-backed e2e for
+      the advance-only path deferred; covered by unit + monotonic SQL.)*
+
+## Review
+
+- Backend `build` + `pnpm verify:fast` green (EXIT=0). 20 new unit tests pass.
+- No frontend change needed: the list already sorts `updatedAt desc`; that
+  value is now stable from Postgres, so the flip disappears. The 5s poll now
+  only refreshes editor avatars.
+- Migration `20260710000000_add_document_updated_at` adds the column + backfill.
+
+### Code review (high effort, workflow-backed) — outcomes
+
+Applied:
+- Rename/move now bumps `updatedAt` (`updateDocument` sets `now()`) — a metadata
+  edit floats the doc up; content edits still come via webhook.
+- `rawBody` capture scoped to the webhook path in `main.ts` — no longer retains
+  25MB import buffers on every JSON request.
+- Webhook clamps `issuedAt` to `min(issuedAt, now())` — a clock-skewed future
+  event can't pin `updatedAt` ahead and freeze ordering.
+
+Second review pass (post-fix) — applied:
+- Empty / no-op PATCH no longer bumps `updatedAt` (`updateDocument` skips the
+  bump when `data` is empty), so an empty-body PATCH can't re-sort a doc to the
+  top. Added `document.service.spec.ts` for both branches.
+- Simplified `attachMeta` (`{ ...d, updatedAt: d.updatedAt.toISOString() }`).
+
+Deferred (documented in design Risks):
+- Backfill of pre-deploy Yorkie `updated_at` + self-heal for missed webhooks →
+  reconciliation job (Option C). Low impact now (live admin read already times
+  out ~every poll, so today's list is effectively `createdAt` order); tracked as
+  follow-up.
+- Deploy sequencing (migrate-before-serve, webhook registration) → release
+  runbook items, not code.
+
+## Non-Goals / follow-ups
+
+- Webhook loss self-heal (backend down during edit) — accept small staleness
+  initially; a periodic Yorkie→PG sync (Option C) or read-time touch can be
+  layered later.
+- Live "editing" avatars still use Yorkie presence (decorative; failure no
+  longer affects ordering). Fixing the 800ms admin-query latency itself is
+  separate.
+
+## Verification
+
+- `pnpm verify:fast` green.
+- e2e: signed webhook advances `updatedAt`; unsigned/bad-sig rejected.
+- Manual: list order stable across polls in `pnpm dev`; editing a doc floats
+  it to the top after the next webhook.

+import { Body, Controller, HttpCode, Post, UseGuards } from '@nestjs/common';
+import { SkipThrottle } from '@nestjs/throttler';
+import { DocumentService } from './document.service';
+import { parseYorkieDocKey } from '../yorkie/yorkie-doc-key';
+import { YorkieSignatureGuard } from './yorkie-signature.guard';
+
+/**
+ * Shape of Yorkie's event-webhook body (yorkie 0.7.12,
+ * `api/types/event_webhook.go`). Typed loosely and validated by hand so an
+ * unexpected/extra field never turns into a 4xx — Yorkie retries on failure,
+ * and we would rather swallow-and-200 anything we don't recognize than
+ * trigger a retry storm.
+ */
+interface YorkieEventBody {
+  type?: string;
+  attributes?: { key?: string; issuedAt?: string };
+}
+
+/** The only webhook event type yorkie emits (fired on real root edits). */
+const DOCUMENT_ROOT_CHANGED = 'DocumentRootChanged';
+
+/**
+ * Receives Yorkie document event webhooks and mirrors the last-edit time into
+ * Postgres (`Document.updatedAt`), which is what the documents list orders by.
+ * This is how content edits — which flow client → Yorkie only, never through
+ * this backend — become visible to the list without a per-request Yorkie admin
+ * call. Authenticated by HMAC signature ({@link YorkieSignatureGuard}); not
+ * behind the JWT guard. `@SkipThrottle` so bursts of edit events aren't
+ * rate-limited away.
+ */
+@Controller('internal/yorkie')
+@SkipThrottle()
+@UseGuards(YorkieSignatureGuard)
+export class YorkieEventController {
+  constructor(private readonly documentService: DocumentService) {}
+
+  @Post('events')
+  @HttpCode(200)
+  async handleEvent(@Body() body: YorkieEventBody): Promise<{ ok: true }> {
+    if (body?.type !== DOCUMENT_ROOT_CHANGED) {
+      return { ok: true };
+    }
+
+    const key = body.attributes?.key;
+    const parsed = key ? parseYorkieDocKey(key) : null;
+    if (!parsed) {
+      return { ok: true };
+    }
+
+    // Trust Yorkie's issue time as the edit time, but clamp it to now() and
+    // fall back to now() if missing/unparseable. `touchUpdatedAt` only moves
+    // the time forward, so a clock-skewed *future* issuedAt would otherwise pin
+    // updatedAt ahead and make the monotonic guard reject every later real
+    // edit until wall-clock caught up. Out-of-order / duplicate deliveries stay
+    // harmless.
+    const now = Date.now();
+    const issuedMs = Date.parse(body.attributes?.issuedAt ?? '');
+    const at = new Date(Number.isNaN(issuedMs) ? now : Math.min(issuedMs, now));
+
+    await this.documentService.touchUpdatedAt(parsed.id, at);
+    return { ok: true };
+  }
+}

+import {
+  CanActivate,
+  ExecutionContext,
+  Injectable,
+  Logger,
+  ServiceUnavailableException,
+  UnauthorizedException,
+} from '@nestjs/common';
+import { ConfigService } from '@nestjs/config';
+import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from 'crypto';
+import type { Request } from 'express';
+
+/**
+ * Verifies Yorkie event-webhook requests. Yorkie signs the request body with
+ * `HMAC-SHA256(rawBody, project.SecretKey)` and sends it as
+ * `X-Signature-256: sha256=<hex>` (see yorkie `pkg/webhook/client.go`). The
+ * signing key is the project's secret key, which this backend already holds
+ * as `YORKIE_SECRET_KEY` for the admin service — so no new secret is needed.
+ *
+ * The raw request bytes are captured by the `verify` hook wired into
+ * `bodyParser.json` in `main.ts`; HMAC must run over the exact bytes, not a
+ * re-serialized object.
+ */
+@Injectable()
+export class YorkieSignatureGuard implements CanActivate {
+  private readonly logger = new Logger(YorkieSignatureGuard.name);
+  private readonly secretKey?: string;
+
+  constructor(configService: ConfigService) {
+    this.secretKey = configService.get<string>('YORKIE_SECRET_KEY');
+  }
+
+  canActivate(context: ExecutionContext): boolean {
+    if (!this.secretKey) {
+      // Without the shared secret we cannot authenticate the caller; refuse
+      // rather than trust an unsigned request to mutate `updatedAt`.
+      this.logger.error(
+        'YORKIE_SECRET_KEY is not configured; rejecting event webhook',
+      );
+      throw new ServiceUnavailableException('Webhook verification unavailable');
+    }
+
+    const req = context
+      .switchToHttp()
+      .getRequest<Request & { rawBody?: Buffer }>();
+
+    const header = req.header('x-signature-256');
+    const rawBody = req.rawBody;
+    if (!header || !rawBody) {
+      throw new UnauthorizedException('Missing webhook signature');
+    }
+
+    const expected = `sha256=${createHmac('sha256', this.secretKey)
+      .update(rawBody)
+      .digest('hex')}`;
+
+    const a = Buffer.from(header);
+    const b = Buffer.from(expected);
+    if (a.length !== b.length || !timingSafeEqual(a, b)) {
+      throw new UnauthorizedException('Invalid webhook signature');
+    }
+    return true;
+  }
+}

samples.summary: Unauthenticated, throttle-exempt webhook endpoint accepts up to 25MB bodies — unbounded pre-auth resource consumption
samples.evidence: `@SkipThrottle()` (yorkie-event.controller.ts:32) removes the only global rate limit (ThrottlerGuard registered as APP_GUARD in app.module.ts:113, 120 req/60s). The parameter is annotated with an inline TS type (`@Body() body: { title?: string }`), so the emitted `design:paramtypes` metadata is `Object` and the global ValidationPipe (main.ts:59-66, `whitelist`/`forbidNonWhitelisted`) skips validation entirely — those options only strip properties when the metatype is a decorated DTO class. Prisma accepts any valid `DocumentUpdateInput` at runtime, so an authenticated caller scoped to workspace A can PATCH one of its own documents with e.g. `{"workspace":{"connect":{"id":"<victim-workspace-id>"}}}` (moving attacker-controlled content into a workspace they are not a member of — WorkspaceScopeGuard only checks the route param, not the body), or `{"author":{"connect":{"id":1}}}` to forge authorship, or overwrite `id`/`fileId`. The sibling legacy route (document/document.controller.ts:183-196) does the safe thing and copies allowlisted fields; this one does not. The diff modifies `DocumentService.updateDocument` (document.service.ts:99-101) without narrowing this sink.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as claimed. ApiV1DocumentsController.update (documents.controller.ts:67-81) forwards the raw request body as Prisma `data`. The @Body param is annotated with an inline object type, so the metatype is `Object` and the global ValidationPipe (main.ts:59-66) skips it — no whitelist stripping occurs, and grep shows no other pipe/interceptor (api-v1.module.ts:17-35, no APP_PIPE anywhere). DocumentService.updateDocument (document.service.ts:88-102) spreads that data straight into prisma.document.update typed as DocumentUpdateInput, so nested relation writes are accepted at runtime. The only authorization gate, WorkspaceScopeGuard (workspace-scope.guard.ts:18-37), validates the route param workspaceId only and never inspects the body; the preceding getDocumentOrThrow merely confirms current ownership, not the target of a re-parent. An authenticated caller scoped to workspace A can therefore PATCH its own doc with {"workspace":{"connect":{"id":"<victim>"}}} to push content into a workspace it is not a member of, forge author via {"author":{"connect":{"id":N}}}, or repoint fileId at another workspace's blob. The sibling legacy route (document.controller.ts:183-196) shows the safe allowlist + assertMember(body.workspaceId) pattern that this route omits. Squarely in the authorization/access-control lane and not otherwise guarded.

samples.summary: Nothing in the repo registers the Yorkie project event webhook, so outside the (documented, manual) cluster runbook step `Document.updatedAt` never advances on content edits
samples.evidence: docker-compose.yaml:12 starts `yorkieteam/yorkie:latest` with only `server --pprof-enabled`; no project provisioning, no `--event-webhook-url`/`--event-webhook-events`. Grep for `eventWebhook|event_webhook|EventWebhook` across the repo matches only the comment in packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-event.controller.ts:9. The read path was changed (packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.ts:64) to stop deriving updatedAt from Yorkie, so in every environment where the webhook is not hand-registered (local dev, docker-compose, CI, any deploy that misses the runbook step) the "Modified" column and list ordering silently degrade to creation time — a behaviour regression versus the previous Yorkie-sourced value. docs/design/documents-last-modified.md:63-71,101-104 acknowledges this as a manual ops step only.
searchedFor: glob for k8s/helm manifests via yaml search

samples.summary: Public API v1 document list was not updated for the new ordering contract and now leaks the raw `updatedAt` Date
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/api/v1/documents.controller.ts:29-38 still calls `documentService.documents({ where })` with no `orderBy` and returns the raw Prisma rows. After this change those rows carry the new `updatedAt` column (serialized as a Date/ISO string with different semantics from the internal list's explicitly-mapped `updatedAt`), and the API list ordering is now inconsistent with `/documents` and `/workspaces/:id/documents`, which sort by `[{updatedAt:desc},{createdAt:desc}]` (packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.ts:116,148).

samples.summary: Existing controller unit test still stubs YorkieAdminService with `getSummaries`, which `attachMeta` no longer calls
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.spec.ts:13 constructs the controller with `{ getSummaries: jest.fn() } as never`. `attachMeta` now calls `getEditors` (packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.ts:60), so this double is stale: it only passes because the spec exercises `createDocument`; any list-path test added against it would throw `getEditors is not a function`. The repo already records this exact trap in docs/tasks/archive/2026/07/20260707-documents-list-sort-search-lessons.md:29-30.

samples.summary: Backend env documentation still describes YORKIE_SECRET_KEY as optional and presence-only, though it now also gates the webhook that keeps last-modified ordering correct
samples.evidence: packages/backend/README.md:38-41 says "Optional, project secret key; enables 'currently editing' presence ... Omit and the list still works without avatars." With this change the same variable is the HMAC key for `POST /internal/yorkie/events` (packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-signature.guard.ts:30); when unset the guard 503s every webhook and `updatedAt` never advances, so the list silently loses last-modified ordering — not just avatars.

samples.summary: Frontend doc comment still says the "Last modified" value comes from Yorkie
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/documents/document-list-utils.ts:41 — "The value used for the 'Last modified' column: Yorkie's `updatedAt`, ...". The backend now sources it from the Postgres `Document.updatedAt` column (packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.ts:64); the comment describes the removed contract.

samples.summary: New `Document.updatedAt` sort key has no index, though both workspace list queries now sort on it
samples.evidence: The migration adds only the column; no `CREATE INDEX` on `"Document"("updatedAt")` and schema.prisma has no `@@index`. Both list endpoints now sort by it (packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.ts:116,148), and `touchUpdatedAt` (packages/backend/src/document/document.service.ts:120) issues an `updateMany` per edit webhook, so read+write volume on this column grows with edit traffic.

samples.summary: Integration bootstrap helper does not install the rawBody `verify` hook added in main.ts, so any e2e exercise of the webhook would 401
samples.evidence: packages/backend/test/helpers/integration-helpers.ts:75-84 `applyGlobalBootstrap` applies only the ValidationPipe; it does not mirror the `bodyParser.json({ verify })` capture added at packages/backend/src/main.ts:47-56. Test apps built with it (e.g. packages/backend/test/authenticated-http.e2e-spec.ts:74) therefore never populate `req.rawBody`, and `YorkieSignatureGuard` would reject any signed webhook request as "Missing webhook signature". Fix belongs in the helper (or by moving the bootstrap into a shared function used by both main.ts and the helper).

samples.summary: Webhook route path is duplicated as a string constant in main.ts and as decorators in the controller, coupled only by a comment
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/main.ts:27 hardcodes `/internal/yorkie/events`, which must stay in sync with `@Controller('internal/yorkie')` + `@Post('events')` (packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-event.controller.ts:31,36). Any future `setGlobalPrefix`, path rename, or trailing-slash variation silently stops rawBody capture and turns every webhook into a 401 with no failing test.

verdict.reason: The literal absence is real — I searched repo-wide (all file types), .mjs verify scripts, all GitHub workflows, backend bootstrap (main.ts), YorkieAdminService (GetDocuments only, no UpdateProject), prisma migrations/seeds, and confirmed there are no k8s/helm/deploy manifests anywhere; `event-webhook|project update|UpdateProject` matches only the design doc. However it is not a blocking blast-radius defect. (1) No consumer contract is broken: `updatedAt` is still a non-null ISO string on every list item (document.controller.ts:32-39,64), metadata edits still advance it (document.service.ts:94-100), and no guard is bypassed. (2) The finding's asserted regression ("behaviour regression versus the previous Yorkie-sourced value" in local dev / docker-compose / CI) is contradicted by the code: the old Yorkie-sourced path returns an empty map whenever YORKIE_SECRET_KEY is unset (yorkie-admin.service.ts:84-88), and that key is unset in docker-compose.yaml:12-18, .github/workflows/ci.yml:167-177, and is documented as optional in packages/backend/README.md:36-41 — so those environments already ordered by createdAt before this change. (3) The one environment where it matters (a cluster that sets the secret key) requires provisioning of the external Yorkie project, which is cluster config not held in this repository at all, and is explicitly a release-runbook item (docs/design/documents-last-modified.md:63-71,101-104; docs/tasks/active/20260710-docs-list-updatedat-webhook-todo.md:50-52). That is an ops/deployment-completeness concern for the design-fit/ops lens, not a changed contract with an unupdated caller or a reachable guard bypass.
